questions.stem: Here is the case: Gabriel Bello wants to build a strong credit history over time. Which habit is most reliable for improving a credit score?

options.text: Close the oldest accounts to look more disciplined.
options.misconception: removes useful history and can raise utilization

options.text: Pay every bill on time and keep balances low relative to limits.
Apply for many new cards at once to show borrowing activity.
options.misconception: creates many inquiries that can lower a score

options.text: Carry a balance each month because interest payments build credit.
options.misconception: mistakes paying interest for a scoring benefit

questions.explanation: Payment history and the share of available credit used are central to common scoring models, so paying on time and keeping balances low is reliable. Carrying a balance, closing old accounts, or many applications can hurt rather than help.
questions.hint: On-time payments and low utilization matter most.
